messages:
jordan: Heads-up — LumenBay just opened a support ticket, reporting p99 embeds jumping from ~1s to ~12s starting ~07:10 PST. They say it affects only the prod tenant (tenant:lumenbay-prod) and started after a deploy. sample req id: req_0a1b2c3.

sam: looking. which pool are they on? any reservation id?

jordan: they're on Dedicated pool: ded-usw-3, reservation: res-42b7. Alex from CS pasted the ticket with user repro: curl to /v1/embeddings, model llama2-8b-redwood-v2, batch size 1.

alex-cs: customer says p95 is fine, p99 blows out. they have spikey traffic but claim no recent config changes. requesting an allowlist or higher priority in the pool — asking for a fast workaround, otherwise they threaten to failover. :worried: 

marta: thanks. can you paste the request headers + trace id? I want the trace link.

jordan: trace link: https://observability.redwood/prod/traces/req_0a1b2c3 (last 30s). headers: X-Req-Id:req_0a1b2c3, X-Tenant:lumenbay-prod, Region:us-west.

infra-bot: Alert: high p99 embeddings latency on ded-usw-3 (metric: embeddings.p99 > 6s) — triggered 07:12 PST — top affected tenant: lumenbay-prod (80% samples). CPU on node gtx-a01 at 77%, GPU util 96% on same host, queue depth 23.

sam: GPU 96% + queue depth 23 = noisy neighbor possibility. can ops-sre run per-tenant queue breakdown and identify top token producers in the last 15m?

ops-sre: running query...
```
SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) as tokens, count(*) as reqs
FROM token_logs
WHERE pool = 'ded-usw-3' AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY tokens DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

ops-sre: result: 1) thunderai-prod: 43M tokens, 2) lumenbay-prod: 5.2M tokens, 3) sparrow-ops: 4.9M. thunderai is way higher.

marta: thunderai looks like the noisy neighbor. but infra-bot flagged lumenbay as top affected — that's consistent (they hit the long tail when thunderai saturates). we should verify whether thunderai traffic is batching poorly or sending very long contexts.

sam: can we repro with a synthetic at tenant throttle at the node level? quick mitigations: 1) apply a soft per-tenant concurrency cap for thunderai (e.g., max_concurrency=6) 2) add lumenbay to the priority allowlist so their requests get prefetched/priority in KV cache 3) increase lumenbay's reservation burst for 30m. which is fastest?

alex-cs: customer prefers allowlist over throttling other customers, but understands emergency throttles if we explain. they asked if we can do an allowlist now and follow up with quota changes.

marta: we can push a temporary priority tag to lumenbay on the routing layer — gives KV cache + batching priority for 20 minutes. I'll prepare the command.

marta: command to apply priority tag (run from infra-admin host):
```
# give tenant priority routing for 20m
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/v1/tenants/lumenbay-prod/priority \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
 -d '{"ttl_minutes":20, "priority_level": "high"}'
```

marta: and quick throttle for thunderai (soft):
```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/v1/tenants/thunderai-prod/throttle \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
 -d '{"max_concurrency":6, "mode":"soft", "ttl_minutes":30}'
```

ops-sre: applying priority to lumenbay now. will monitor p99 for next 10m.

infra-bot: Action executed: priority tag applied to tenant lumenbay-prod TTL=20m by marta.

ops-sre: also applied soft throttle to thunderai-prod (max_concurrency=6) to reduce GPU contention. monitor link: https://observability.redwood/dashboards/queue/ded-usw-3

sam: checked traces after actions — lumenbay p99 dropped from ~12s -> ~1.6s within 90s of changes. thunderai queue depth dropped from 23 -> 6. Good short-term outcome.

jordan: passing note to CS: "LumenBay — temporary priority + throttle applied; latency returned to normal. We will follow up with permanent options."

alex-cs: customer acknowledged: "Thanks, we see it improved. Please advise long-term fix."

marta: long-term options to propose to customer and product: 1) dedicated reservation increase (res-42b7++) 2) tenant isolation via stricter pool partitioning for high token producers 3) fair-share scheduling improvements (we have a draft) 4) per-tenant adaptive caching (project ask).

ops-sre: created incident runbook entry: INCIDENT-2026-03-17-LUMENBAY-TAIL. Actions recorded: priority-tag applied, soft-throttle applied, observed metrics improved. Owner: marta.

sam: follow-ups for eng-runtime: please dig into batching patterns for thunderai; check if they send a mix of very long contexts causing KV pressure. assign to @marta for initial triage and escalate to @eng-runtime if we see systemic kernel contention.

marta: I found thunderai has many long-context batches (>4096 tokens) in last hour; KV cache miss rate went up. I'm leaving a note in the ticket: adding tenant-level prefetch and cache-ttl tuning could mitigate.

jordan: next steps for CS: offer lumenbay a 30-day priority trial or recommend reservation bump. I'll draft email.

alex-cs: sent to customer: "We applied a temporary routing priority and reduced noisy-tenant concurrency. Latency restored. We'll follow up with long-term proposals and a timeline." :email:

ops-sre: monitoring will keep alerting for 2h; I've scheduled a 30m post-mortem with eng/runtime + product tomorrow 09:00 PST.

marta: closing this Slack thread, keeping incident open until PM/eng follow-up. ping me if latency resurges. :thumbsup:
